Cada vez son más las personas que alcanzan una edad avanzada. Se prevé que el número de personas mayores de 65 años se duplique en todo el mundo en las próximas décadas y alcance la cifra estimada de 1.600 millones en 2050. A las personas mayores se las considera con demasiada frecuencia dependientes de las demás. Se las ve como receptoras de ayudas sociales y benéficas, en lugar de como titulares de derechos capaces de tomar decisiones por sí mismas. Durante un conflicto armado, la violencia afecta de forma desproporcionada a las personas mayores, pero a menudo no se las tiene en cuenta en las respuestas humanitarias. Durante la pandemia de COVID-19, los gobiernos aplicaron políticas que ocasionaron miles de muertes evitables en residencias de todo el mundo. Además, estas decisiones crearon niveles de aislamiento social sin precedentes entre las personas mayores. La protección de los derechos humanos de las personas mayores a menudo es débil y, a veces, inexistente. Amnistía Internacional hace campaña para que se ponga fin a la discriminación por motivos de edad y se elaboren leyes que protejan los derechos de las personas mayores. The Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA) establishes reporting and recordkeeping requirements for employers and labor relations consultants. Pursuant to the LMRDA, this agency, the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS), has established the Form LM-10 Employer Report and Forms LM-20 and 21 consultant reports, on which the parties must report concerning agreements or arrangements to persuade employees concerning their rights to organize and bargain collectively or supply an employer with information concerning the activities of employees or a labor organization in connection with a labor dispute involving the employer. An employer must file a Form LM-10 concerning other matters as well, including for expenditures made with an object to commit an unfair labor practice or to obtain information concerning the activities of employees or a labor union involved in a labor dispute. The transparency created by these requirements is designed to better inform workers in making determinations regarding the exercise of their rights to organize and bargain collectively. Pertussis CHIM Biorepository Dec. 2, 2025 Key points Scientists recently developed a pertussis controlled human infection model (pertussis CHIM). The aim was to build a foundation for and accelerate development and licensure of next-generation pertussis vaccines in the United States. Biological samples from this pertussis CHIM are available for researchers. Request samples by following the application process. Overview The first North American pertussis CHIM study began enrolling participants in July 2022. The objective of this study was to establish a pertussis CHIM. Researchers aimed to identify a Bordetella pertussis challenge dose that could safely and reproducibly achieve mild, symptomatic infection in healthy adults aged 18–40 years. The B. pertussis strain (D420) used in this study was a well-characterized strain obtained from a U.S. infant with pertussis. The Canadian Center for Vaccinology, located in Halifax, Canada, established the CDC-supported North American pertussis CHIM platform. Global impact Pertussis remains one of the leading causes of vaccine-preventable deaths worldwide, despite overall high vaccination coverage. Most pertussis deaths occur in young babies who are either unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated . Trends In 2024, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported 941,565 pertussis cases globally. Between 1990 and 2019, the global number of new cases of pertussis annually declined 40.98%. A 2014 publication estimated 24.1 million pertussis cases and 160,700 deaths in children younger than 5 years worldwide. Foley – named after the pioneerng Warner Brothers sound engineer Jack Foley – is the art of creating sounds in sync with the picture, from footsteps and rustling clothes to the movements of creatures. CHICAGO -- Pete Crow-Armstrong broke into a smirk, thinking back to the last time his mom played the role of catcher so he could throw some practice pitches in their yard. pages.text: Pete Crow-Armstrong wins 2026 NL MVP unanimously Skip to Content CHICAGO – During the final home game of this past season, a considerable number of fans in Wrigley Field’s bleacher seats were waving green flags . Pete Crow-Armstrong did not have to look hard to spot them as he made his way out to center field that afternoon, and he later admitted feeling a bit overwhelmed by it all. Those flags – featuring the made-for-chanting “M-V-Pete” rallying cry – were in celebration of a season for the ages from the Cubs’ star. They also served as a prediction. Crow-Armstrong’s multiple-month surge turned a conversation into a debate and, finally, into the only possible outcome on Thursday night. Crow-Armstrong is the National League’s Most Valuable Player. “It tends to be hard for me to process things right after they happen,” Crow-Armstrong said, “especially something like this, where I’m really just feeling lucky.” All-time MVP Award winners By the time the smoke had cleared on Crow-Armstrong’s incredible 2026 campaign, the only question, really, was whether he would take home the MVP in unanimous fashion . The voting body of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America answered that with 30 first-place nods , giving the Cubs center fielder an MVP victory unlike any in team history. Crow-Armstrong is the first unanimous MVP for the Cubs, whose previous winners since the BBWAA began handing out the award in 1931 were Kris Bryant (2016), Sammy Sosa (1998), Andre Dawson (‘87), Ryne Sandberg (‘84), Ernie Banks (1958-59), Hank Sauer (‘52), Phil Cavarretta (‘45) and Gabby Hartnett (‘35)

History In 2010, a paper map by 3dShapes was digitized and imported, to map landuse in Nederland. The import project was well conducted and properly documented in the OSM-wiki. This was a major step in filling in the space on OSM. Some problems remained after import, to be dealt with later. For instance, where trees had been planted in multiple rows, it was imported as an orchard. As a result, our motorways were suddenly lined with orchards, on OSM-based maps. This has been fixed by organized mappings. Another example: the paper map had a tile grid of thin black lines. These lines were seen as cut lines, resulting in unnecessary and awkward splits of the imported areas. The import procedure did detect this problem, but couldn’t automate a fix, so this was left to the future mappers. It took 15 years before a crazy mapper got rid of this in a solo project lasting 2 months. Guess who? pages.text: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peter Storey won 19 caps for England Published 17 November 2026 Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. "We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund." Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield. He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions. Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72. pages.text: PhD Student Workshop on Microeconomic Policies & Economic Growth | NBER Skip to main content PhD Student Workshop on Microeconomic Policies & Economic Growth March 31, 2027 — Washington, DC Share X LinkedIn Facebook Bluesky Threads Email Link While the high-level goal of encouraging economic growth is a key macroeconomic objective of many policymakers, many of the policy levers linked to growth—such as facilitating housing construction or expanding energy infrastructure—involve microeconomic policies. Research often falls short in generating the type of evidence of interest to policymakers. Microeconomic researchers who study these policies often focus on economic efficiency or the distributional consequences of potential reforms, rather than estimating the extent to which these policies affect economic growth. To fill this gap, the Smith Richardson Foundation is supporting a project which includes a series of nine studies of the economic growth consequences of changes in microeconomic policies such as incentives for R&D investment and expedited permitting for energy and transportation infrastructure. That project is co-led by Pete Klenow (Stanford University), Ken Kuttner (Williams College), and Heidi Williams (Dartmouth College), and is engaging with economists at several non-partisan federal agencies—such as the Federal Reserve, the Congressional Budget Office, and the Joint Committee on Taxation. He previously served as the Acting Deputy Director and Division Director for Outreach and Business Development (OBD), where he led efforts to source quality project applications. Prior to joining DOE, Mr. Kangas spent 25 years in the private sector as a management consultant, including a 20+ year career at Grant Thornton LLP, where he led the firm’s National Energy Advisory practice for clients in the natural resources, mining, and renewables sectors. He also led the federal sciences portfolio for work delivered at DOE, Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), National Science Foundation (NSF), and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Ongcal/ICRC Armed conflicts have become the defining feature of our time. There are about 130 armed conflicts happening globally, marking a huge increase compared to the number recorded 15 years ago. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook The nature of fighting has evolved—they have become longer and more destructive . During conflicts, the rules that aim to protect civilians— international humanitarian law (IHL) —have been bent, dismantled or ignored altogether. Meanwhile, in the Philippines, we have observed that although fighting has not completely ended, there has been a noticeable reduction in hostilities. In some areas, the humanitarian consequences of decades of armed conflicts can still be felt by the people. In these places, farmers and fishermen displaced by fighting are unable to sustain their livelihoods; they may still be harassed or live in fear because of pressure from warring parties. During and after conflicts, civilians often pay the highest price. It is for this reason that the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has been on the front line for humanity since 1863 , working to preserve human dignity and relieve human suffering whenever war or armed violence strikes. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook In the Philippines, sporadic clashes still occur, although hostilities have generally decreased in Mindanao. As a result, remote communities are displaced or cut off from their farms and other sources of livelihoods. They lose access to reliable and safe water and sanitary facilities, as well as other essential services due to their displacement. But even when fighting has ended, such as in the 2017 Marawi conflict, humanitarian consequences linger. Around 300 families are still searching for their missing relatives and struggling with systemic socioeconomic challenges. Meanwhile, the country’s jails and prisons remain overcrowded despite the authorities’ efforts to improve conditions of detention and vulnerability to natural hazards. Prisoners are often losing contact with loved ones. The situation in the Philippines demonstrates that even when fighting becomes intermittent, it still leaves a significant impact on vulnerable communities. A Kermode bear, also called a spirit bear, rests in British Columbia's mossy Great Bear Rainforest, where heavy rainfall and mild temperatures support lush green vegetation. The spirit bears are a rare subspecies of black bear, found only along Canada's Pacific coast, with a recessive genetic mutation that causes their ghostlike white fur. Photographs by Paul Nicklen Text by Annie George Published July 28, 2026 In his 30 years as a photographer and cinematographer, Paul Nicklen has experienced it all—from living on the sea ice, to surviving plane crashes and dislocated shoulders, to sleeping many nights under the stars. And in this unpredictable wilderness, he finds the deepest sense of peace. "It’s always been the reverence I have for nature. I mean, I don’t want to get too religious or anti-religious, but that's my church, and that's where I find everything makes sense,” Nicklen told National Geographic. “I've had nothing but reverence for nature since I was a little kid." Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble? 23 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Liv McMahon , Technology reporter and Osmond Chia , Business reporter How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk? For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. To help understand the mechanisms behind and consequences of this variation, the NBER Center for Aging and Health Research is planning a conference on place, aging, and health. The conference, which is made possible by support from the National Institute on Aging, will be organized by Alee Lockman (Texas A&M University) and Sarah Miller (University of Michigan and NBER). It will be held in Cambridge, Massachusetts, on Friday, September 17, 2027 . To understand the relationship between place and aging, the meeting will focus on several factors with the potential to shape the health and well-being of older adults, including rurality, the expansiveness of Medicaid home- and community-based services, and the robustness of long-term care infrastructure.
